$comment: Reviewed exceptions to the origin check (SEC-054; scripts/supply-chain/origin-check.ts). Each entry names the package whose code is excused (found through the source maps), the rule, optionally a path prefix in the bundle and a text the finding must contain, the reason, the decision record and an expiry date (YYYY-MM-DD) after which the check fails again. The two PDF.js entries are accepted by owner decision 67 (docs/owner-decisions-2026-11-15.md). The sandboxed extension entry is the one exception 10 section 3.8 foresees, accepted by owner decision 120. The MathLive entry is a text, proposed in ADR 0410 and waiting for the owner.

exceptions.reason: PDF.js's fallback for a frame without workers imports GlobalWorkerOptions.workerSrc on the main thread (build/pdf.mjs, _setupFakeWorkerGlobal). The viewer sets workerSrc to the URL of its own bundled worker, resolved against its own location (packages/element/src/pdf/viewer/main.ts, startWorker), so the address is a file of the viewer on the viewer's origin. The viewer runs in a sandboxed frame of its own (10 §3.1). Valid only while the viewer sets workerSrc that way.

Without WebAssembly, PDF.js's worker imports a JavaScript decoder from the wasmUrl the document was opened with (build/pdf.worker.mjs, WasmImage #getJsInstance: jbig2_nowasm_fallback.js, openjpeg_nowasm_fallback.js). The viewer passes wasmUrl as ./pdfjs/wasm/ resolved against its own location (packages/element/src/pdf/viewer/main.ts, open), where the build copies those files from pdfjs-dist. Valid only while the viewer sets wasmUrl that way.

The runtime inside the sandboxed frame of a tier 2 extension (packages/ui/src/extensions/sandbox-runtime.ts) loads the extension's entry as a classic script from the address the host configured. It is the one place in the editor's code that creates a script element, and it runs only in a frame with an opaque origin, no network and no handle on the host page (docs/review/2026-11-18-ux-060-sandbox-review.md). The frame page's own policy (script-src) is the host's, and the extension's code is not part of the editor bundle or its bill of materials.

The address is inside the text of a console.error message that MathLive prints when the CortexJS Compute Engine is not loaded (it tells the developer how to load it). MathLive reads the engine from globalThis[Symbol.for('io.cortexjs.compute-engine')] and never imports the address; the editor does not load the engine. Valid only while that stays the one use of the address in MathLive.
